instruction: Switch Ubuntu to Do Not Disturb mode so notification banners are silenced.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent clicked the notification area in the top panel to open the notification/calendar panel, then toggled the 'Do Not Disturb' switch at the bottom of the panel to enable DND mode. The task completed in 4 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can click the top panel notification area, interact with the notification/calendar panel, and toggle UI switches
metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling Do Not Disturb mode on Ubuntu, which sets org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-banners to false. Evaluator checks this gsettings key for the value 'false'.
metadata.task_rationale: Direct rephrasing of the original successful task; uses standard check_include_exclude metric on the gsettings output to verify DND is enabled.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly runs 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-banners' which directly reads the GNOME setting controlling notification banner visibility — exactly the right state to verify Do Not Disturb mode.
Metric 'check_include_exclude' receives the rules dict directly (via get_rule returning config['rules']), accesses rules.get('include', []) correctly — no parameter handling errors.
Expected value 'false' matches what gsettings outputs when show-banners is disabled; substring check 'false' in 'false\n' is True — semantically correct.
Setup config pre-sets show-banners to true, ensuring initial state fails evaluation — good negative control resistance.
Single-requirement instruction is fully covered by a single evaluator check — complete coverage.
gsettings is a persistent system setting; no UI dialog needs to be open, so no postconfig is required.
